as_reported: AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution

records.label: Large FBH kindred (5 generations)

phenotypes.text: elevated serum immunoreactive PTH in adults, supranormal by about age 30
lower serum inorganic phosphate than unaffected relatives
radiographic changes suggestive of osteomalacia in affected adults over 40
defective skeletal mineralization on iliac crest biopsy

quotes: Of the 46 individuals studied, 19 were found to be affected. Serum iPTH levels, determined in three separate immunoassays, became supranormal by about age 30 years in the group of 15 hypercalcemic subjects examined biochemically and appeared to increase further thereafter.

Three of five affected adults older than age 40 years who were studied radiographically had changes suggestive of osteomalacia. Biopsy of the iliac crest of one of the subjects, a 51-year-old woman, confirmed the presence of defective skeletal mineralization.
Serum alkaline phosphatase activity and creatinine levels were normal in these individuals, but inorganic phosphate levels were lower than in unaffected kindred members.

records.label: Oklahoma kindred

phenotypes.text: developmental elevation in serum parathyroid hormone levels

quotes: A five-generation kindred (19 affected, two obligate carriers and 20 unaffected) from Oklahoma USA, in which familial benign (hypocalciuric) hypercalcaemia (FBH) was associated with a developmental elevation in serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels

records.label: Oklahoma family (FBHOk)
records.segregation: Linked to chromosome 19q13 (max LOD 6.67 at D19S606); linkage to 3q and 19p excluded
quotes: in an Oklahoma family with an FBH variant (FBHOk), for which linkage to 3q and 19p had been excluded
Linkage was established between FBHOk and eight chromosome 19q13 loci, with the highest LOD score, 6.67 (recombination fraction.00), obtained with D19S606.

phenotypes.text: low calcium to creatinine clearance ratio
elevated serum PTH in adults >30 years

records.segregation: FBHHOk segregated with a chromosome 19q13 haplotype; peak LOD 6.92 at D19S606; recombinants in II.2, III.3, III.4 define interval D19S112-rs245111
quotes: Thus, the 34 family members from five generations included for genetic analysis of the FBHH3 locus consisted of 19 affected members, 13 unaffected members and 2 unaffected spouses (Figure 1).

Elevated concentrations of serum PTH had been observed in some affected individuals >30 years of age (II.2, II.4, II.6, II.9 and III.6, Figure 1). Three adults >40 years of age (II.4, II.9 and III.3) also showed evidence of osteomalacia.
the biochemical phenotype of FBHH was established by documenting hypercalcaemia associated with a low ratio (<0.01) of calcium clearance to creatinine clearance.

Sixteen members were hypercalcemic with normal or elevated serum PTH concentrations and mild hypophosphatemia, features consistent with FHH3.

records.label: Japanese female infant
quotes: This Japanese female infant was found to have hypercalcemia by a routine laboratory test for poor weight gain on breast feeding. At 49 days of age, serum calcium (adjusted by Payne's formula) was 13.1 mg/dL, intact PTH 27 pg/mL, and urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio 1.29 mg/mg.

Although no pathologic mutation was detected in CASR or GNA11, a presumably de novo heterozygous mutation (p.Arg15Leu), a previously reported causative mutation for FHH3, was identified in AP2S1 of this patient.

records.label: Proband (34-year-old woman)

variants.as_reported: AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution

quotes: The probands included a 34-year-old woman who had a 12-year history of hypercalcemia. She presented with fatigue, headaches, and persistent generalized aches that did not resolve after parathyroidectomy.
Each of the three probands had an AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution (Fig. 1A).

Each of the three probands had an AP2S1 mutation causing an Arg15Cys, Arg15His, or Arg15Leu substitution (Fig. 1A).

notes.statement: Howles et al. (2016) found that cinacalcet (10 nM) corrected the abnormal intracellular calcium signaling and MAPK responses to extracellular calcium in cells expressing the calcium-sensing receptor together with the FHH3-associated Cys15, His15, or Leu15 AP2-sigma mutants.
quotes: Cinacalcet (at a concentration of 10 nM) corrected the abnormal intracellular calcium signaling and MAPK responses to extracellular calcium in cells expressing the Cys15, His15, or Leu15 AP2-sigma mutants

notes.statement: Howles et al. (2016) treated 3 unrelated probands with FHH3 due to AP2S1 Arg15 mutations with oral cinacalcet (30 to 60 mg daily) for 33 to 45 months, resulting in more than 20% reductions in serum calcium and abatement of symptoms, with increased serum phosphate and reduced PTH remaining in the normal range. No nausea, vomiting, or hypocalcemia developed, although the authors noted that long-term surveillance would be required.
quotes: Oral cinacalcet (at a dose of 30 to 60 mg daily) was administered to the three probands with familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia type 3 over a 33-to-45-month period. This treatment led to more than 20% reductions in serum calcium concentrations (Fig. 1B) and abatement of symptoms.
Adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, and hypocalcemia did not develop in any of the probands. However, long-term surveillance will be required to assess safety and monitor for hypocalcemia.

notes.statement: Fujisawa et al. (2013) found that their infant with FHH3 showed catch-up growth on a low-calcium formula (2.6 mg/dL calcium), with lower serum calcium and a lower urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio. A 2:1 mixture of low-calcium and standard formula kept serum calcium at about 12 mg/dL without a marked rise in PTH. The authors suggested that low-calcium formula is worth trying in infants with FHH.
quotes: With use of low calcium formula containing 2.6 mg/dL of calcium, she showed catch-up growth, and serum calcium was decreased, as was urinary calcium-to-creatinine ratio.
Furthermore, feeding with a mixture of low calcium formula and standard formula with a 2:1 ratio maintained serum calcium ∼12 mg/dL without markedly increasing serum PTH.
low calcium formula is worth attempting in infants with FHH

notes.statement: Fujisawa et al. (2013) concluded that a lack of hypocalciuria does not necessarily argue against an AP2S1 mutation. They suggested that their patient's early infantile age played a part in her hypercalciuria.
quotes: The results imply that lack of hypocalciuria does not necessarily argue against the presence of AP2S1 mutations. The early infantile age of this patient would have played a certain role in the occurrence of hypercalciuria

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) performed exome sequencing in an affected individual from each of two unrelated FHH3 kindreds (FHH3OK and FHH3NI) and, within the 3.46-Mb FHH3 interval on 19q13.3, found a single shared variant, a C-to-T transition in exon 2 of AP2S1 predicting an Arg15Cys missense change, which cosegregated with the disorder.
quotes: An analysis of SNVs within the 3.46Mbp interval on 19q13.3, which is the location of the FHH3 locus, and contains ~110 genes, revealed one SNV, a C to T transition in exon 2 of the AP2S1 gene

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) sequenced AP2S1 in 50 unrelated FHH patients without CASR mutations and found 11 heterozygous missense mutations, all affecting Arg15 (4 Arg15Cys, 3 Arg15His, 4 Arg15Leu), suggesting that AP2S1 Arg15 mutations may cause FHH in more than 20% of patients without CASR mutations and that Arg15 is a likely mutational hotspot.
quotes: This revealed the occurrence of 11 missense heterozygous mutations, consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance of FHH3, that all affected Arg15 and consisted of four Arg15Cys, three Arg15His, and four Arg15Leu mutations
Indeed, Arg15 AP2S1 missense mutations may be the underlying cause of FHH in >20% of patients without CaSR mutations.

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) found that patients with the different AP2S1 Arg15 mutations, aged 8 days to 78 years, had similar elevations in serum calcium and PTH and reductions in urinary calcium excretion, indicating no correlation between the specific mutation and the clinical phenotype.
quotes: had similar elevations in serum calcium and PTH concentrations and reductions in urine calcium excretion, thereby indicating an absence of a correlation between the mutation and clinical phenotype

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) found that in HEK293 cells stably expressing CaSR, all three AP2S1 Arg15 mutants (Cys, His, Leu) caused a rightward shift in the concentration-response curve with significantly higher EC50 than wildtype, indicating reduced sensitivity to extracellular calcium; the Cys15 mutant gave an EC50 higher than vector alone, suggesting a possible dominant-negative effect.
quotes: This revealed that expression of all three mutant AP2σ2s led to a rightward shift in the concentration–response curves (Fig. 3c-e) with significantly higher EC50
thereby indicating a possible dominant-negative effect for this AP2S1 mutant

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) showed that, after calcium stimulation, cells transfected with wildtype AP2S1 had greater reduction of cell-surface CaSR than cells transfected with the Arg15Cys mutant, indicating reduced CaSR endocytosis; Arg15 contacts the glutamine at position -4 of dileucine motifs, and mutating the CaSR C-terminal dileucine motif (Leu-Leu1013-1014 to Ala-Ala) also increased EC50, suggesting that the mutants act through loss of interaction with this motif.
quotes: cells transfected with wild-type AP2S1 had a significantly further reduction of cell-surface CaSR expression when compared to those transfected with mutant Arg15Cys AP2S1 or vector alone
Thus, these results indicate that the CaSR dileucine motif is functionally significant.

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2013) noted that FHH3 is characterized by clinical features different from FHH1 and FHH2, including increased serum PTH concentrations, hypophosphatemia, and osteomalacia.
quotes: FHH3 is characterised by different clinical features, which include increased serum PTH concentrations, hypophosphatemia, and osteomalacia,.

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2010) studied 24 members across 3 generations of a kindred with FHH whose proband had no CASR mutation. FHH cosegregated with chromosome 19q13.3 markers, with a peak lod score of 5.98 at 0% recombination with D19S412. Analysis of recombinants placed the locus in a 3.46-Mb interval between SNP rs1990932 on the centromeric side and D19S604 on the telomeric side.
quotes: Use of microsatellite and single nucleotide polymorphic loci from chromosome 19q13.3 demonstrated cosegregation with FHH in the kindred, with a peak LOD score = 5.98 at 0% recombination with D19S412.
Analysis of recombinants mapped FHH to a 3.46-Mbp interval flanked centromerically by single nucleotide polymorphism rs1990932 and telomerically by D19S604.

notes.statement: Nesbit et al. (2010) noted that FHH is genetically heterogeneous, with 3 types: FHH1 (3q21.1), FHH2 (19p), and FHH3 (19q13). FHH1 is caused by CASR mutations and accounts for more than 65% of patients. They suggested that FHH3 may explain the disorder in FHH patients without CASR mutations.
quotes: FHH1, caused by mutations of the calcium-sensing receptor (CASR), occurs in more than 65% of patients, whereas the abnormalities underlying FHH2 and FHH3, which have each been described in single North American kindreds, are unknown.
FHH3 may explain the calcium homeostasis disorder in those FHH patients who do not have CASR mutations.

notes.statement: Hannan et al. (2010) performed linkage studies with 24 polymorphic loci in the 5-generation Oklahoma kindred and obtained a peak LOD score of 6.92 at zero recombination with D19S606. Recombinants refined the FBHH3 locus to a 4.1-Mb interval on 19q13 flanked by D19S112 and rs245111, containing 135 protein-coding genes and 24 predicted genes.
quotes: Linkage between FBHHOk and 10 of the 14 polymorphic loci (Table 1) from chromosome 19q13 was established with the highest peak LOD score of 6.92, at 0% recombination, being observed between D19S606 and FBHHOk.

Thus, the FBHH3 was mapped to an interval flanked centromerically by D19S112 and telomerically by rs245111. This interval was found to be 4.1 Mb in size and to contain 135 protein-coding genes and 24 predicted genes.

notes.statement: Hannan et al. (2010) sequenced the coding regions and intron-exon boundaries of 12 candidate genes from the FBHH3 interval that were expressed in parathyroid and/or kidney (including PTH2, PTGIR, GNG8, EMP3, SPHK2, TULP2, NUCB1, HRC, RCN3, CYTH2, RRAS, ATF5) in an affected individual and found no abnormalities; RT-PCR excluded splicing defects.
quotes: DNA sequence analysis of the coding region and intron–exon boundaries of these 12 genes, from an individual affected with FBHHOk and from an unrelated normal individual, did not detect any abnormalities. In addition, RT-PCR excluded any splicing abnormalities, thereby indicating that these genes were unlikely to be responsible for FBHHOk.

notes.statement: Hannan et al. (2010) found that the region syntenic to the FBHH3 interval on mouse chromosome 7 contains 4 Casr-related sequences (Gprc2a-rs), but no human homologs exist; comparative analysis showed that 2 conserved segments were inverted and an 11.6-Mb region containing 35 murine genes, including the 4 Gprc2a-rs genes, was absent from the human genome, so FBHH3 cannot be attributed to these genes.
quotes: However, a bioinformatic (BLAST) analysis of the human 19q13 region did not identify the human, or primate, homologues of the Gprc2a-rs genes, thereby precluding their mutational analysis for FBHH3.
In addition, an 11.6 Mb region on mouse chromosome 7 that contains 35 murine genes including the four Gprc2a-rs was not present in the human genome (Figure 3).

notes.statement: In a genomewide search in an Oklahoma family with a variant of familial benign hypercalcemia (FBHOk), in which linkage to 3q and 19p had been excluded, Lloyd et al. (1999) found linkage to 8 chromosome 19q13 loci, with a maximum lod score of 6.67 at theta = 0.0 for D19S606. Recombinants placed the locus in an interval of less than 12 cM flanked by D19S908 and D19S866.
quotes: Linkage was established between FBHOk and eight chromosome 19q13 loci, with the highest LOD score, 6.67 (recombination fraction.00), obtained with D19S606.
Recombinants further mapped FBHOk to a <12-cM interval flanked by D19S908 and D19S866.

notes.statement: Lloyd et al. (1999) found no abnormalities in the coding region, 5-prime UTR, or part of the promoter of the calmodulin III gene, which lies within the candidate interval, in an individual affected with FBHOk, indicating that this gene is unlikely to be involved.
quotes: The calmodulin III gene is located within this interval, and DNA sequence analysis of the coding region, the 5' UTR, and part of the promoter region in an individual affected with FBHOk did not detect any abnormalities, thereby indicating that this gene is unlikely to be implicated in the etiology of FBHOk.

notes.statement: Lloyd et al. (1999) noted that not all patients with familial benign hypercalcemia have CaSR mutations and that another locus had been mapped to 19p13.3; the Oklahoma variant, excluded from 3q and 19p, mapped to 19q13, showing a third locus.
quotes: However, not all FBH patients have CaSR mutations, which, together with the mapping of another FBH locus to 19p13.3, suggests that additional CaSRs or second messengers may be involved.

notes.statement: Trump et al. (1995) studied a 5-generation Oklahoma kindred with FBH and developmental elevations in serum PTH. Using 17 polymorphic markers, they excluded linkage to 3q21-q24 and 19p13.3 (FBH loci), 11q13 (MEN1) and 11p15 (PTH), with lod scores below -2.00 at theta = 0.05-0.25. Multipoint crossover analysis and LINKMAP confirmed the exclusion.
quotes: By means of 17 polymorphic markers from these regions, linkage was excluded [LOD scores < -2.00 at (theta) = 0.05-0.25].
In addition, an analysis of multipoint crossovers and use of the LINKMAP program confirmed the exclusion from these regions.

notes.statement: Trump et al. (1995) named this form of FBH the Oklahoma variant, FBH(Ok). They concluded that their results indicated further genetic heterogeneity and a third locus for FBH.
quotes: Thus, this form of FBH, designated the Oklahoma variant FBH(Ok), is not linked to markers that segregate with FBH, MEN1 and PTH; our results indicate further genetic heterogeneity and the presence of a third locus for FBH.

notes.statement: McMurtry et al. (1992) noted that in their kindred, FBH in adults could be especially difficult to distinguish from primary hyperparathyroidism because serum iPTH levels may be elevated.
quotes: In this kindred, FBH in adults can be especially difficult to distinguish from primary hyperparathyroidism because serum iPTH levels may be elevated.

notes.statement: McMurtry et al. (1992) concluded that the disorder in their kindred may not be totally benign: osteomalacia, perhaps due to mild hypophosphatemia, can develop during adulthood. They raised the possibility that they had observed an unusual variant of FBH.
quotes: Furthermore, the disorder may not be totally benign. Osteomalacia, perhaps due to mild hypophosphatemia, can develop during adulthood.
will help to clarify if we have observed an unusual variant of FBH
